# Alex Batten

> Freelance .NET and full-stack software engineer based in Denmark. Available for
> new freelance and contract work. Typical work: backend services, REST APIs,
> enterprise and tax-authority integrations, multi-tenant SaaS, Stripe billing, and
> AI features. Remote across the EU on CET.

Alex Batten holds a BEng in Software Technology from the Technical University of
Denmark (DTU). Most of his work is in C# and .NET with full-stack web, API and
enterprise integrations, and AI/ML data work. He publishes three .NET libraries on
NuGet under the Invarix name and speaks English and Danish.

Contact: alex.batten1234@gmail.com

## Current work

- **Senior Software Engineer, AI Infrastructure at Alignerr** (contract signed
  2026, first assignment pending): the agreed scope is the infrastructure behind
  AI training, evaluation, and deployment pipelines, in Python and TypeScript.
- **AI Engineer & Co-Owner at Acconta** (2026 to present): full-stack work on a
  multi-tenant Danish bookkeeping SaaS, from microservices in .NET Aspire,
  ASP.NET Core, and EF Core on Azure to the Next.js client. Took Danish VAT
  reporting to SKAT from the NemVirksomhed (RSU) SOAP integration (WS-Security
  signing, all 17 VAT return fields) to the Next.js screens and SKAT's
  production gateway. Built the bank reconciliation backend on an open banking
  feed (Aiia) and upgraded SAF-T import and export to the 2.1 schema ahead of
  the 2027 audit-file mandate. Owns Stripe billing end to end. Leads e-invoicing
  over NemHandel and Peppol (OIOUBL, Peppol BIS), turns the Bookkeeping Act and
  its executive orders into implementation specs, and does most of the team's
  in-depth code review. Set up an autonomous AI development agent (an OpenAI
  dot) built to take GitHub issues and run Codex agents that implement, review,
  and test each change before a human reviews the pull request.
- **Generalist Danish Annotator at Mercor** (2026 to present): writing prompts in
  Danish on topics of general interest and annotating how AI models respond.
- **Generalist Expert, AI Evaluation at Mercor** (2026 to present): evaluating AI
  model outputs against structured guidelines and writing the rationale behind
  each judgment.
- **AI Data Annotator at Outlier** (2025 to present): data annotation, prompt
  engineering, agentic trajectory design, and QA across 50+ risk categories.

## Published software

- [Invarix.Guard](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Invarix.Guard): A plug-and-play
  AI safety library for .NET. Covers prompt injection, PII, and content safety so
  applications can add guardrails in a few lines of code.
- [Invarix.Guard.Evidence](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Invarix.Guard.Evidence):
  A tamper-evident audit trail for AI decisions in .NET, free under Elastic
  License 2.0. Records decisions as CloudEvents keyed on SHA-256 hashes, seals
  batches into an RFC 6962 Merkle tree signed with the customer's own Ed25519 key,
  and runs fully in process with no outbound calls.
- [Invarix.Gate](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Invarix.Gate): A deterministic action
  firewall for AI agents in .NET. Evaluates an agent's tool calls against a policy
  before they run and returns allow, warn, escalate, deny, or terminate. Ten detectors
  covering destructive SQL, shell commands, git history rewrites, cloud teardown,
  credential egress, and runaway loops, each grounded in a dated public incident. Pure
  CPU pattern matching with no model call, median verdict 57 microseconds, deterministic
  under a given policy. Policy as YAML or fluent C#, with adapters for
  Microsoft.Extensions.AI and Microsoft Agent Framework. Observe mode is free under
  Elastic License 2.0. Currently 1.0.0-rc.1.
